target.title: [AI-assisted] Tidy Android Sessions row affordances
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves The Android Sessions screen mixed a loose text action and circular row markers with the compact boxed visual language used elsewhere. The sort action lacked a clear tap boundary, while session markers and status indicators made row geometry feel less consistent when scanning the list. ## Why This Change Was Made This keeps the cleanup intentionally visual and local to `SessionsScreen.kt`. The sort action now uses a compact outlined surface, the session marker uses a small rounded-square container with aligned icon sizing, and visible status indicators are grouped into a fixed compact slot. Sorting, layout switching, selection, filtering, and session data behavior are unchanged. ## User Impact The Sessions screen now has clearer control boundaries and more consistent row geometry without adding density or changing workflows. Sort and layout interactions continue to behave as before. ## Evidence Real environment: OpenClaw Android Play debug app running on the lane-e API 36 emulator and paired with an isolated local OpenClaw Gateway. Before and after captures were taken only after the app reported Gateway Online, Nodes 1/1, Approvals 0, zero pending device and node approvals, and one paired node. **Online state verification**
Before After
Validation: - `node scripts/ensure-cli-startup-build.mjs` passed. - Baseline `pnpm android:assemble` passed: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` in 2m 41s. - Patched `pnpm android:assemble` passed: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` in 2m 33s. - `git diff --check` passed. - The same Sessions interactions were exercised before and after: Sort toggle, Layout compact/default, and Sort toggle again.
Before After
**Before interaction video** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b410c720-ebe9-484a-9768-9c9a9415aff2 **After interaction video** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f6d23a1-2e9c-4075-a499-e469ebefb60e The videos are serial-bound ADB screen recordings, not image sequences. `ffprobe` reported H.264 1080x2400, 7.47 seconds / 72 frames before and 11.72 seconds / 67 frames after. Extracted frames were inspected for stable target-screen coverage and private-data leaks. No automated UI test was added because this change only adjusts Compose geometry; runtime behavior was verified on the paired emulator.
